chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from al-Mundhar al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah, who said:
Verily, this Ummah will not be ruined until they speak about their Lord.
ai.seo_question: What condition prevents the ruin of the Ummah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah suggests that the community remains in a state of theological vitality and is not yet doomed to ruin as long as it engages in *kalam* (discursive theology) regarding Allah’s nature. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that active intellectual inquiry, even when leading to debate, is preferable to the stagnation of ignorance, serving as a sign that the faith is still being actively understood and articulated.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 16. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (RA) said: `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far said Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub said, on the authority of `Amr ibn Abu alMiqdam, on the authority of Salim ibn Abu Hafsah, on the authority of Mundhar al-Thawri, that Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah said:
“Verily, this Ummah will not be ruined until they stat discussing (the nature of) their Lord.”
